In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polysomes of relaxed cells are more resistant to phenylalanine deprivation than those of the stringent strain.

in stringent cells the breakdown of polysomes is a rapid process, and is not accompanied by any change in the distribution of newly-formed RNA between the soluble and membrane fractions of the cell, whereas in relaxed cells polysome breakdown occurs slowly and is associated with a marked increase in the quantity of 4 S RNA found in the extracts.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in stringent cells, the RNA formed during phenyalanine starvation is mainly 16 S RNA, whereas in relaxed cells, the RNA is mainly 4S and is not connected with the ribosomes.

the stringent cells respond to phenylalanine deficiency by rapidly decreasing the rate of protein synthesis and by rapidly degrading the polysomes, whereas the relaxed cells do not respond by decreasing the rate of synthesis, but by decreasing the amount of RNA released into the extract.
polysomes are more stable and the synthesis of RNA is more efficient in stringent than in relaxed cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polysome breakdown in stringent and relaxed cells is a two-stage process.
the stringent response is a global response that affects the entire cell.
stringent and relaxed strains differ in their responses to phenylalanine-starvation, and that this difference is not due to differences in the synthesis or degradation of RNA.
